findings.title: Saving Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of parsed data corrupts Google Calendar credentials
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` call which returned the parsed credential object directly. Passing `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })` overwrites the stored credential `key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`. On the next instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService`, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail because the top-level keys (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc.) are now nested under `data`, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration after its first token refresh.

findings.title: Invalid computed property keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` do not match dynamic expiry properties
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances, which produces `"[object Object]"`. This defines a schema that requires a literal `"[object Object]"` property with a numeric value and strips all other properties beyond `access_token` (such as `expiry_date` or `expires_in`). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will always fail on normal token responses and throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

findings.title: `prisma` is not imported and refreshed Salesforce access token is not used by the connection
findings.body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `@calcom/prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever `SalesforceCalendarService` is instantiated. (2) Even before that, the refresh request is not wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and on line 106 the `jsforce.Connection` is initialized with the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the ID of the `Credential` row) as the third argument `userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, which will look up the wrong user.

findings.title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` that is incompatible with callers expecting SDK/axios return shapes
findings.body:
When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a standard `fetch` `Response` object. Several callers pass SDK or axios callbacks that return different structures and immediately access properties that do not exist on a `fetch` `Response`:
- `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (`googleapis` response format).
- `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) treats the return value directly as a `HubspotToken` (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`) and saves the raw `Response` object to `prisma.credential.update`.
- `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `tokenInfo.data` (`axios` response format).

For all four integrations, token refresh will fail or write an invalid `key` to the database when credential syncing is enabled.

findings.title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name, not `app.slug`, breaking webhook for several apps
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by the app directory name (e.g., `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, `zoomvideo`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` and `appMetadata.slug` use the config slug (e.g., `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`, `zoom`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` returns `undefined` for all of these apps, causing the webhook to return 404 `"App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"` even when a valid `appSlug` is provided.

findings.title: Inconsistent `appSlug` `"zoomvideo"` passed to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: Zoom's app slug in `config.json` and the database is `"zoom"` (as used in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` line 63: `appId: "zoom"`), but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called here with `"zoomvideo"`. The sync endpoint receiving `appSlug` will get `"zoomvideo"` during token refresh while the webhook endpoint `/api/webhook/app-credential` requires `"zoom"`.
